question: What are the main Medicare plan options available to seniors age 65 and older in 2027?
transcript_excerpt: There are two main types of plans: Medicare supplements, which allow you to go to any doctor or hospital with no preexisting conditions and no need for referrals, and Medicare Advantage HMO products, which are more robust than under-65 HMO products but require you to select a specific physician group and work within that team network.

question: What are the 2027 Medicare Part D prescription drug deductible and out-of-pocket maximum changes?
transcript_excerpt: The prescription drug deductible has increased from $615 to $700, though some plans may offer a lower deductible. The maximum out-of-pocket cost has risen from $2,100 to $2,400, which is the amount individuals actually pay; once this limit is reached, beneficiaries pay nothing more for the rest of the year.

question: How many standalone prescription drug plans are available in California for 2027?
transcript_excerpt: In California, there are now only 10 standalone prescription drug plans available for 2027, compared to 15 that were previously offered, requiring many seniors to switch plans after receiving plan termination letters.

question: When is the annual open enrollment period for Medicare and what coverage changes can beneficiaries make?
transcript_excerpt: The annual open enrollment period runs from October 15th to December 7th. During this time, beneficiaries can change standalone prescription drug plans, change Medicare Advantage HMO plans, leave HMO plans to apply for Medicare supplements, or switch from Medicare supplements to HMO plans.

question: What is the Medicare Part B late enrollment penalty structure for those who delay enrollment?
transcript_excerpt: The penalty is 10 percent for every 12 months you are not covered under Part B, and this penalty applies for the rest of your life. You have seven months to sign up around your birthday—three months before, the month of, and three months after your birthday.
